reports.title: Yukon Main Estimates (Operation and Maintenance and Capital Estimates)
reports.description: Annual Main Estimates setting out the Government of Yukon's planned operation-and-maintenance and capital expenditures and revenues for the fiscal year, prepared under the direction of Management Board for the Legislative Assembly.

reports.title: Yukon Fiscal Outlook (and companion Economic Outlook)
reports.description: Annual fiscal and economic outlook documents accompanying the Yukon Budget that project revenues (including federal transfers), expenditures, surplus/deficit and net debt over a multi-year horizon.

reports.title: Northwest Territories Main Estimates and Budget Address / Fiscal Review
reports.description: Annual Main Estimates, Budget Address and Fiscal Review papers setting out the Government of the Northwest Territories' planned revenues (including the Grant from Canada), operating expenditures and fiscal outlook.

reports.title: Nunavut Main Estimates and Fiscal and Economic Indicators / Budget
reports.description: Annual Main Estimates, Budget Address and Fiscal and Economic Indicators documents setting out the Government of Nunavut's planned revenues (Territorial Formula Financing and other federal transfers), expenditures and fiscal outlook.

reports.title: Yukon Bureau of Statistics
reports.publisher: Yukon Bureau of Statistics (Government of Yukon)
reports.description: Territorial statistical agency that compiles and publishes Yukon-specific population estimates, economic accounts, labour-force indicators, CPI for Whitehorse, retail sales and annual statistical reviews, drawing on Statistics Canada data and its own surveys.

reports.title: NWT Bureau of Statistics
reports.publisher: NWT Bureau of Statistics (Government of the Northwest Territories)
reports.description: Territorial statistical agency responsible for the NWT statistical program; publishes population estimates, GDP, labour-force activity, CPI, community statistics and socio-economic scans, frequently using Statistics Canada source data.

reports.title: Nunavummit Kiglisiniartiit (Nunavut Bureau of Statistics)
reports.description: Nunavut's central statistical agency; collects, analyses and disseminates population, labour-force, CPI (Iqaluit), GDP and community statistics for the territory, operating under the Statistics Act (Nunavut) and partnering with Statistics Canada.

reports.title: Yukon Public Accounts (Financial Statement Discussion and Analysis and Consolidated Financial Statements)
reports.publisher: Yukon Department of Finance / Office of the Comptroller
reports.description: Annual audited Public Accounts of the Government of Yukon, including the Financial Statement Discussion and Analysis that reports actual revenues (formula financing grant, CHT, CST) and the consolidated financial statements.

reports.title: Northwest Territories Public Accounts (Consolidated Financial Statements and Financial Highlights)
reports.description: Annual Public Accounts of the Government of the Northwest Territories, including consolidated financial statements that detail the Territorial Formula Financing Grant, its calculation basis (Gross Expenditure Base, eligible revenues) and the share of total revenue represented by federal transfers.

reports.title: Nunavut Public Accounts (with Financial Statement Discussion and Analysis)
reports.description: Annual Public Accounts of the Government of Nunavut, including the Financial Statement Discussion and Analysis that reports actual Territorial Formula Financing receipts and their year-over-year change.

reports.title: Yukon Statistical Review
reports.description: Annual statistical compendium prepared by the Yukon Bureau of Statistics covering population, labour force, earnings, CPI, GDP by industry, retail trade, tourism and other indicators, drawing heavily on Statistics Canada data.

reports.title: Northwest Territories Lands and Resources Devolution Agreement
reports.publisher: Government of Canada / Government of the Northwest Territories / Aboriginal Parties
reports.description: The 2013/2014 devolution agreement transferring administration and control of public lands, waters and non-renewable resources to the NWT, defining Resource Revenues, Net Fiscal Benefit, and the offset against Territorial Formula Financing payments.

reports.title: Nunavut Lands and Resources Devolution Agreement
reports.publisher: Government of Canada / Government of Nunavut / Nunavut Tunngavik Incorporated
reports.description: The 2024 final devolution agreement transferring administration and control of public lands, freshwater and non-renewable resources to Nunavut, with a transfer date of 1 April 2027 and resource-revenue sharing provisions that interact with Territorial Formula Financing.

reports.title: Northwest Territories Intergovernmental Resource Revenue Sharing Agreement
reports.publisher: Government of the Northwest Territories / Aboriginal Parties
reports.description: Agreement under which the GNWT shares up to 25% of its Net Fiscal Benefit from resource revenues with participating Aboriginal governments, in addition to existing land-claim royalty shares.

NWT Bureau of Statistics population releases are based on Statistics Canada estimates. The document states: "On April 1, 2026 Statistics Canada estimated that 45,808 people were living in the Northwest Territories."

The Financial Statement Discussion and Analysis of the Yukon Public Accounts states that the majority of revenues come from the formula financing grant and quantifies the federal share of total revenue. The document states: "The Government’s revenue is largely made up of the formula financing grant from the Government of Canada, which tends to remain stable over time. ... In 2025, the Government received 81.7% of its revenue from the Government of Canada ... In 2025, the Government received $1.350 billion from the formula financing grant, an increase of $98.0 million (7.8%) from the previous year."

The Yukon Public Accounts schedule of revenues and the Discussion and Analysis list the Canada Health Transfer as a distinct federal transfer. The document states: "The Canada Health Transfer was $59.5 million, and the Canada Social Transfer was $19.3 million."

The Yukon Public Accounts schedule of revenues and the Discussion and Analysis list the Canada Social Transfer as a distinct federal transfer. The document states: "The Canada Health Transfer was $59.5 million, and the Canada Social Transfer was $19.3 million."

The NWT Public Accounts Consolidated Financial Statements and notes explain the Territorial Formula Financing Grant as the difference between the Gross Expenditure Base and eligible revenues, and report that federal grants and transfer payments constitute 73.1% of revenue. The document states: "The Territorial Formula Financing Grant is an annual formula-based calculation based on a three-year moving average of data, which includes a two-year lag, to fill the fiscal gap between the Government’s expenditure needs and its ability to raise revenues. The NWT’s Grant equals the difference between its Gross Expenditure Base and a measure of revenue capacity known as eligible revenues. ... The Government’s largest source of revenue is the grant and transfer payments from Canada which represent 73.1% of revenue for the current year."

The Nunavut Public Accounts Financial Statement Discussion and Analysis reports the actual Territorial Formula Financing amount and its year-over-year change as the primary driver of federal revenue growth. The document states: "Revenues from the Government of Canada rose by 2.1% ($54.7M), driven by a 7.0% ($138.0M) increase in Territorial Formula Financing, which reflects the formula’s annual adjustment to address rising public service costs. ... Territorial Formula Financing 2,109,474"

NWT Bureau of Statistics GDP pages state that Statistics Canada releases the annual GDP estimates for the Northwest Territories that the Bureau republishes and analyses. The document states: "Statistics Canada releases annual estimates of GDP for the Northwest Territories and other provinces and territories."

The NWT devolution agreement defines the Resource Revenues that are subject to offset against the Territorial Formula Financing Payment, and Canada’s TFF page confirms the exclusion of natural-resource revenues from the TFF calculation in favour of the devolution arrangements. The document states: "“Net Fiscal Benefit” means the amount of Resource Revenues that is not offset against the Territorial Formula Financing Payment pursuant to sections 10.2 and 10.3."

NWT budget and Public Accounts documents reference the devolution agreement’s resource-revenue sharing and the resulting reduction in the Territorial Formula Financing Grant. The document states: "Half of resource revenues are shared with the federal government by reducing the Territorial Formula Financing Grant payments from Canada to the Government of the Northwest Territories."

NWT fiscal documents record the net fiscal benefit transfer to Indigenous government signatories under the intergovernmental resource-revenue sharing arrangement. The document states: "Net Fiscal Benefit Transfer to Indigenous Government Signatories ... Contribution to NWT Heritage Fund"

Canada’s TFF page notes that negotiations with Nunavut on the treatment of natural-resource revenues are ongoing; the 2024 Nunavut devolution agreement now supplies the framework that will govern those revenues once the April 2027 transfer occurs. The document states: "Negotiations with the Government of Nunavut are ongoing."
